problem: CDK2 atom-to-node assignment QUBO, 3 anchor atoms x 4 pocket nodes
bit_order_convention: AWS Braket: leftmost character is qubit 0. Under the reversed convention the best sampled energy is -373.7957 with 1 shot at the exact ground state, but that single hit sits inside the 6.1% random-luck band, so the mean is the statistic to rely on.
headline: On a real 20-qubit superconducting QPU the best of 256 shots reached -373.69, matching the noiseless simulator's best at the same shot count and within 0.03% of the certified ground state. The mean energy of +295 is far below the +784 expected from uniform random sampling, so the circuit carries real algorithmic signal despite 244 distinct outcomes in 256 shots.
honest_caveats: 244 distinct bitstrings from 256 shots means the output distribution is heavily noise-broadened; this is a NISQ-era result, not a clean one.
No shot landed exactly on the ground state under the Braket bit convention.
The reduced 12-qubit instance is 3 atoms x 4 nodes, not the full 54-variable docking QUBO.
